title: feat(migrations): idempotent runner with backfill for existing deployments
body:
## Summary

Replaces the manual `docker exec -i $DB_CT psql -f migration.sql` workflow with `scripts/apply-migrations.sh` — an **idempotent runner** that tracks state in `public.schema_migrations(version, applied_at)` and only runs migration files whose filename is not yet recorded.

**Why now**: this is foundational work for upcoming PRs (next_invoice_number, soft-delete) which will ship new migrations. With the runner in place, those migrations apply automatically on a single command instead of requiring a per-migration `docker exec` call from the user, reducing the chance of skipping a migration or applying one twice.

### What's new

- `scripts/apply-migrations.sh` — host-side bash script that:
  - Auto-detects the `db` container via the Compose service label (`com.docker.compose.service=db`), works for both `docker compose` and Coolify. Falls back to a name pattern, or `DB_CONTAINER=<name>` override.
  - Ensures `public.schema_migrations(version text primary key, applied_at timestamptz)` exists.
  - **Backfill safety net**: on first run, if `schema_migrations` is empty BUT `public.invoices` already exists (= existing production that has been getting manual migrations), inserts every current filename as already applied — without re-running any SQL.
  - Applies pending files in lexical order. Stops on first failure WITHOUT recording the failed file, so re-running retries cleanly.
- README updated with the new workflow.

### What's NOT in this PR

- No changes to existing migrations.
- No new SQL.
- No changes to Dockerfiles or `docker-compose.yaml`.

So this is safe to merge alone — production state isn't touched until the operator runs `./scripts/apply-migrations.sh` once.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] Verify `./scripts/apply-migrations.sh` runs cleanly on the existing Coolify deployment. Expected output on first run:
  ```
  Using db container: db-v5xudtj41ezyw-...
  First run on an existing schema detected.
  Backfilling public.schema_migrations without re-running any SQL.
  Backfilled 19 versions.
  All migrations up to date — nothing to apply.
  ```
  If auto-detect fails, pass `DB_CONTAINER=<name>` explicitly.
- [ ] Confirm `select count(*) from public.schema_migrations;` returns 19 after the backfill (one row per file in `supabase/migrations/`).
- [ ] Re-run the script — should print `All migrations up to date — nothing to apply.`
- [ ] Quick smoke test on a fresh DB if convenient: `docker compose down -v && docker compose --env-file .env.selfhost up -d` — the existing initdb path still applies all migrations as before; `schema_migrations` is created by this runner the first time it's invoked.

### Test plan I ran locally

Spun up `postgres:15-alpine` with the compose service label and ran:

1. **Fresh DB** — applied 4 migrations until `pg_cron` (not present in vanilla postgres image) caused the 5th to fail. Failed migration was correctly NOT inserted into `schema_migrations`. ✓
2. **Drop schema_migrations, re-run** (simulating an existing deployment) — backfilled 19 rows, didn't re-run anything. ✓
3. **Re-run** — `All migrations up to date`. ✓
4. **Add a fake new migration file** — only the new file was applied. ✓
5. **Auto-detect via service label** — worked without `DB_CONTAINER=` override. ✓

### Notes

- Each migration file is piped to `psql` as-is (no implicit `BEGIN/COMMIT` wrapper) so files containing `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE` (e.g. `20260412100000_expand_frequencies.sql`) keep working — Postgres forbids those inside a transaction.
- This means a partial-failure inside a single migration file leaves the DB in the same state as the manual `psql -f` workflow you've been using; not worse, not better.
- Future work (out of scope for this PR): a `db-migrate` Compose service with `profiles: ["migrate"]` so deployments can run `docker compose --profile migrate up db-migrate` instead of needing the host script. Easy follow-up once we agree this is the direction.

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/e9b0f1176ec949b1a476a70f942140fa
Requested by: @jotamano
